description: Never call a food safe; state what the guidance says and link it. Exact kitchen numbers in F and C: the federal minimum internal temperature for poultry, ground meat, beef, bison, goat, pork, lamb, veal, ham, rabbit, venison, fish, egg dishes and leftovers with rest times, and a shellfish visual check that has no number; fridge and freezer keeping times for about 40 foods; the curing salt limit (the federal 156 ppm figure only); the high-altitude boiling point. Answers that are trade practice say so: brine and quick-pickle ratios, coffee and tea ratios, baker's percentages, recipe scaling, and ingredient swaps with allergy flags and a one-line why. Pass topic (temperature, storage, baking, ratio, substitute) or just a query and the topic is inferred. Use for 'is 160 F enough for chicken', 'how long do leftovers keep', 'scale this to 12 servings', 'brine for a 2 kg chicken', 'egg-free swap'. Not medical advice. For nutrition and recalls use check_food; for a full recipe's nutrition use plan_recipe.

amount.description: For ratios: the water or liquid (brine, pickle, coffee, tea) or the meat weight (dry brine, cure)

avoid.description: Allergens to avoid; swaps that list them are flagged and sorted last

food.description: The food, tea type or ingredient, e.g. 'chicken', 'salmon', 'buttermilk', 'green tea'

ingredients.description: For baking scale or percent: the recipe's ingredients with amounts. Weigh flour and water in g, oz or lb for percentages

kind.description: For baking: scale, percent (baker's percentages and hydration) or altitude. For ratio: wet_brine, dry_brine, pickle, cure, coffee or tea

query.description: The question in the person's words, e.g. 'how long does cooked rice keep'

reading_c.description: A thermometer reading in C to compare with the food's minimum

reading_f.description: A thermometer reading in F to compare with the food's minimum

topic.description: Which kind of answer; inferred from query or the other fields when left out

unit.description: Unit for amount: g, kg, oz, lb, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup or floz
